name: lxi-tools
desc: Open source tools for managing network attached LXI compatible instruments
why: Talks to network-attached lab instruments over LXI, a door into a test equipment protocol few developers have touched.

brief.what_it_is: lxi-tools is an open source command-line tool (lxi) and GUI (lxi-gui) for talking to network-attached test instruments that speak LXI, such as oscilloscopes, power supplies, spectrum analyzers and multimeters. It can discover instruments on the local network via VXI11 or mDNS, send SCPI commands and print the responses, capture display screenshots from supported instruments, benchmark request/response speed, and run Lua scripts that control instruments, log data to CSV and draw live charts. All communication goes through the liblxi library.
brief.why_it_exists: The README's stated motivation is 'To make better and simpler open source tools for managing network attached LXI compatible test instruments.' It is an independent community effort and the README says it is not affiliated with the LXI Consortium.
brief.how_it_works: The tools use liblxi for all instrument communication. Discovery broadcasts on each local interface (or uses mDNS/DNS-SD with the -m flag), and SCPI goes over VXI11 (port 111) or raw TCP (port 5025 by default). Screenshots are handled by per-instrument plugins, which can be chosen by name or autodetected, and the image can be written to stdout for piping into other tools.

commands_seen.context: Searches the local network for LXI devices; the README example shows broadcasts on lo, eth0 and wlan0 and lists two Rigol devices found by IP.
Sends the standard *IDN? identification query to the instrument at that IP and prints the response.
Captures a screenshot from a Rigol 1000z oscilloscope using the named plugin and saves a PNG file.
Writes the screenshot to stdout and pipes it into ImageMagick's convert to produce a JPG.
Lists the built-in screenshot plugins, covering Keysight, LeCroy, Rigol, Rohde & Schwarz, Siglent and Tektronix models.
Sends 100 ID requests to the instrument by default and reports requests per second (the README example shows 24.7).
Homebrew install command given in the README for macOS and Linux.
First step of building from source; the README says the install steps may differ by system.
Second step of building from source, compiling the build directory created by meson setup.
Final step of building from source, installing the built files.

brief.install_notes: Besides brew, the README lists distro packages, a snap (snap install lxi-tools, with --edge for bleeding edge), a Windows installer marked experimental, and WSL2 using the snap inside Ubuntu. Building from source needs liblxi, libreadline, liblua, libgtk, libadwaita, gtksourceview and bash-completion; meson_options.txt controls which features are enabled. No instrument accounts or hardware-specific setup is mentioned beyond the instrument being on the network.
brief.standout: It covers a niche protocol family (LXI over VXI11 or raw TCP) with a single CLI and GUI, and its Lua scripting lets you log instrument data to CSV and draw live charts. The README's tested-instrument table is long and specific, and the screenshot plugin system is an easy way to pull a scope's display into a file.
brief.status: unknown. The README shows CircleCI build, release, Repology and CodeFactor badges, links to a releases page and a wiki, names Martin Lund as maintainer, and says it was tested on many current instruments. I saw no release date or last-commit date in the fetched text, so I cannot confirm how recently it was updated.
brief.caveats: The Windows installer is marked experimental in the README. The Tektronix 2000 screenshot plugin is marked experimental. The README says it is not affiliated with the LXI Consortium. The instrument table lists what was tested, not everything that works, and some instruments need RAW/TCP on a specific port rather than discovery. Source builds need several GUI and runtime libraries (GTK, libadwaita, Lua) and the README warns the meson steps may differ by system. The licence is BSD-3-Clause. The screenshot pipe example depends on ImageMagick being installed separately.
